_metadata.description: Approximate, publicly reported figures for major US retailers, compiled from each company's most recent full-year annual report / earnings release available at time of writing. Figures are rounded and intended for illustrative comparison only. Always verify against the latest 10-K before making decisions.

units.revenue_usd_billions: Total revenue / net sales, USD billions
units.net_income_usd_billions: Net income (attributable to company), USD billions
units.store_count: Approximate number of physical stores / warehouses

walmart.name: Walmart Inc.
walmart.business_model: Omnichannel mass-merchant and grocery leader with an everyday-low-price strategy, plus Sam's Club membership warehouses and a large international business.
walmart.membership_program: Walmart+ (subscription: free delivery, fuel discounts, streaming perk)
walmart.ecommerce_highlights: Global e-commerce surpassed $100B in annual sales; store-fulfilled same-day delivery and a fast-growing third-party marketplace.
key_strengths: Unmatched store footprint (most Americans live within ~10 miles of a store)
key_challenges: Competing with Amazon on e-commerce speed and selection
Labor costs at very large scale

amazon.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
amazon.business_model: E-commerce marketplace and logistics network, with highly profitable cloud (AWS) and advertising businesses. Physical retail includes Whole Foods Market and Amazon Fresh.
amazon.membership_program: Amazon Prime (subscription: fast shipping, video, music, and more)
amazon.ecommerce_highlights: Largest US e-commerce player by share; third-party sellers account for the majority of units sold.

costco.name: Costco Wholesale Corporation
costco.business_model: Membership warehouse club with limited SKUs, bulk packs, and low markups; membership fees drive a large share of profit.
costco.membership_program: Costco Gold Star / Executive membership (annual fee, ~90%+ renewal rate in US/Canada)
costco.ecommerce_highlights: Smaller digital share than peers, but growing double digits; big-ticket items and delivery partnerships.
key_strengths: Exceptional member loyalty and renewal rates

target.name: Target Corporation
target.business_model: General merchandise retailer focused on style, owned brands, and convenience; stores act as fulfillment hubs for digital orders.
target.membership_program: Target Circle (free loyalty) and Target Circle 360 (paid same-day delivery)
target.ecommerce_highlights: Most digital orders fulfilled by stores (Drive Up, Order Pickup, same-day delivery).
key_challenges: More discretionary mix makes it sensitive to consumer spending

kroger.name: The Kroger Co.
kroger.business_model: Largest traditional US supermarket operator with multiple regional banners, pharmacies, and fuel centers.
kroger.membership_program: Kroger Plus card (free loyalty) and Boost (paid delivery membership)
kroger.retail_media_network: Kroger Precision Marketing (powered by 84.51 data science)
kroger.ecommerce_highlights: Pickup and delivery, including automated fulfillment centers.
key_challenges: Price competition from Walmart, Costco, and discounters

home_depot.name: The Home Depot, Inc.
home_depot.business_model: Largest home-improvement retailer serving DIY consumers and professional contractors (Pros); expanded into specialty distribution via SRS.
home_depot.membership_program: Pro Xtra (free loyalty program for professionals)
home_depot.ecommerce_highlights: Interconnected retail: a large share of online orders are picked up in store.
key_strengths: High margins relative to general retail
key_challenges: Sensitive to housing market and interest rates
